summary: Pinned-session redispatched to stable variant after edge reshuffle during canary surge
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (BetaBank) reported intermittent responses from the stable variant (v1.2) while they had a session pinned to v1.3 during an active canary rollout of v1.4. Behavior began during a traffic surge and coincided with a recent edge proxy scale event.

Impact:
- A subset of pinned sessions (~0.7% of requests for this tenant during a 12-minute window) returned outputs from an older stable variant, causing correctness regressions for some transactions.
- Customer workflows that assume deterministic model versioning saw mismatched outputs and manual reconciliation.

Timeline (UTC):
- 2026-03-10 14:02: customer first reports inconsistent outputs (chat transcripts attached).
- 2026-03-10 14:05: support triaged and opened this ticket.
- 2026-03-10 14:07: edge-autoscaler reported a scale-up event in us-east due to CPU spike.
- 2026-03-10 14:11: spike subsided; edge pool reconciliation ran and some connection handoffs occurred.
- 2026-03-10 14:14: BetaBank continues to see mixed variants; support captures request/response headers.

Steps to reproduce (internal):
1) Recreate a dedicated tenant with pinned-session header set to v1.3 (sticky cookie + affinity token).
2) Start a steady stream of requests (50 RPS) then inject a short surge (200 RPS for 2 minutes) to trigger edge scale.
3) Observe routing via router trace and verify if any requests are routed to v1.2 stable variant.

Observed behavior:
- During the edge scale-down/reshuffle, the session affinity token persisted but routing table entries were temporarily stale on a small subset of edge nodes. Requests that hit those nodes were forwarded to a fallback stable cluster (v1.2) rather than the pinned runtime (v1.3).

Expected behavior:
- Pinned sessions should be honored across edge scaling events; requests must be consistently routed to the pinned model variant until pin TTL expires or explicit unpin.

Relevant logs and traces (snippets):
- Edge proxy trace IDs: trace-ff12a3b4, trace-ff12a3f9 (see attached).
- Router decision log: "tenant=betabank | session=abc123 | desired_variant=v1.3 | node_view=v1.2,fallback=true | decision=fallback"
- Serving runtime returned header: "x-model-version: v1.2" for several requests with cookie session=abc123.

Temporary customer workaround requested:
- Customer asked for a short-term mitigation: force all traffic to dedicated pool (bypass edge LB) or increase pin-affinity TTL. We approved increasing TTL for BetaBank to 30 minutes while we investigate.

Attachments referenced: request/response headers, minimal repro script, trace links, and sampling of model outputs (omitted here).

2026-03-10 14:16 Priya Nair (SRE): Confirmed edge scale event at 14:06; several nodes rejoined the pool and reported stale routing cache for tenant betabank for ~90s. Pushing for router cache invalidation metrics.
2026-03-10 14:30 Diego Alvarez (Eng): Initial hypothesis: race between edge node reconciliation and router's pin-table updates. Adding instrumentation to log pin-table commit timestamps on edges.
2026-03-10 15:05 Sara Holt (BetaBank): We see ~15 requests in our audit log that returned older templates; increasing TTL helped immediately. Pls keep us posted on root cause.

2026-03-11 09:22 Diego Alvarez (Eng): Reproduced in staging with synthetic surge and confirmed that when node view is applied before pin-table sync, routing falls back. Draft PR ready to add explicit pin republish on node join (see PR link).
2026-03-13 11:40 Priya Nair (SRE): Rolling mitigation queued: backfill a short-lived reconciliation job on node join to ensure pin-table is eagerly synced; will roll to us-east edge pool first.
investigation_notes:
Hypothesis: Edge node join/reshuffle path currently relies on eventual pin-table propagation. Under surge-induced frequent joins, a small timing window allows router decision to treat missing pin as a missing affinity and fall back to stable variant. Evidence: repeated correlation between node join timestamps and fallback decisions; pin-table commit lag observed up to 120s in worst-case.

Observed that the fallback decision path prefers stable variant when pin info absent rather than delaying. This is a tradeoff for latency but causes correctness regressions for pinned sessions.

Instrumentation added: pin-table commit timestamps on edges, decision path logging enhanced to include "pin_lookup_ts" and "node_join_ts". A staged repro in staging reproduced the issue with ~0.6% error rate mirroring production window.

Proposed short-term mitigation: 1) increase default pin TTL for impacted tenant (approved). 2) deploy an eager pin re-sync on node join that blocks routing for that tenant for up to 500ms to allow pin-table catch-up.

Proposed long-term fix: change router decision to prefer waiting up to a configurable threshold for pin-table resolution instead of default fallback; add robust pin-table replication (gossip + immediate push on topology changes).
resolution:
Workaround implemented: increased pin TTL for BetaBank and scheduled an urgent rollout of eager pin resync on node join to us-east edge pool (canary first). Engineering PR: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/4567 contains implementation for immediate pin push on node join and additional metrics.

Next steps: 1) Monitor error rate for BetaBank for 24 hours post-rollout. 2) If stable, roll mitigation globally and schedule follow-up to implement decision-path change to prefer short-block over fallback. 3) Add automated test that simulates edge reshuffles during canary to prevent regressions.

Status: mitigation in progress; patch is in review and canary deploy scheduled for 2026-03-14.
